fuse.name: E_DLOAD_DISABLE
fuse.description: OEM Optional. Disables emergency download via removable SD and/or USB downloader in Apps PBL error handler.

fuse.name: ENUM_TIMEOUT
fuse.description: OEM optional. BOOT ROM must support USB enumeration timeout. Timeout applies to both enumeration for FLCB (fast low current boot) and USB download mode. If USB is not enumerated within time (90 seconds), quit USB enumeration If USB suspend or disconnected after enumeration, start timer again.

fuse.name: FORCE_DLOAD_DISABLE
fuse.description: OEM optional. If FORCE_DLOAD_DISABLE is '0', device goes to download mode if an error occurs very early in XBL1. If FORCE_DLOAD_DISABLE is set to '1', device goes into cold boot if an error occurs very early in XBL1.

fuse.name: FORCE_USB_BOOT_DISABLE
fuse.description: OEM optional. If this bit is 0: FORCE_USB_BOOT GPIO when high during boot up, forces boot from USB. If this bit is 1: it disables this feature and FORCE_USB_BOOT GPIO works as a standard GPIO.

fuse.name: FAST_BOOT
fuse.description: These fuses are used by boot code to specify which device has priority to be booted from. For SM6150, the mapping is as follows: [Default]: 00000: eMMC --> SDC2 --> USB 00001: SDC2 --> eMMC 00010: SDC2 00011: USB 00100: UFS 00101: SDC2 --> UFS Rest Undefined.

fuse.name: SW_FUSE_PROG_DISABLE
fuse.description: This fuse disables the ability to write fuses through the software interface.

fuse.name: SPDM_SECURE_MODE
fuse.description: Indicates that the SPDM must use secure mode. This disables SPDMs from monitoring bus traffic. Since this is a fuse it is permanent.

fuse.name: WDOG_EN
fuse.description: Combined with GPIO Wdog disable (connects to MPM). Prevents the Watch Dog from being disabled by the GPIO.

fuse.name: PBL_LOG_DISABLE
fuse.description: Software only use for boot. Control logging mechanism in boot ROM (If blown, logging is disabled and mandated for external parts).

fuse.name: PBL_USB_TYPE_C_DISABLE
fuse.description: 0: QMP PHY receives CC_OUT (0 - SS Lane1 or 1 - SS Lane2) 1: QMP PHY receives 0 due to PORT SELECT MUX as default value 0 - selects SS Lane1.

fuse.name: ROOT_CERT_TOTAL_NUM
fuse.description: Defines the number of additional root certificates used to sign images containing multiple root certificates (MRC). For example, specify a value of 1 if images are signed with 2 root certificates and specify a value of 3 if images are signed with 4 root certificates. Do not blow if images are signed with a single root certificate.

fuse.name: IMAGE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLE
fuse.description: This bit when blown, is used to indicate that the QTI and OEM Encryption key regions will be used to store the image encryption root keys. When this bit is unblown, these regions will not be used. Note that this bit only enables the image encryption feature, and is NOT an encryption enforcement bit. With image encryption enabled, the chip can boot with either encrypted or plaintext images (the image has meta-data to indicate if the image is encrypted or not).

fuse.name: DISABLE_ROT_TRANSFER
fuse.description: This fuse permanently disables root of trust transfer.

fuse.name: SW_ROT_USE_SERIAL_NUM
fuse.description: If set, PBL checks that signature covers a serial number that matches that read from fuses. This is for secure boot authentication.

fuse.name: USB_SS_DISABLE
fuse.description: Used to disable USB SS enumeration during Boot.

fuse.name: APPS_HASH_INTEGRITY_CHECK_DISABLE

fuse.name: MSS_HASH_INTEGRITY_CHECK_ENABLE

fuse.name: DEBUG_DISABLE_IN_ROM

fuse.name: PBL_EDL_RESET_FEATURE_ENABLE

fuse.name: DEBUG_POLICY_DISABLE

fuse.name: SEC_KEY_DERIVATION_KEY
fuse.description: This 256-bit value is used as the secondary key derivation input; used to generate the secondary key used by the crypto engine. When running insecure (no secure boot; or Debug enabled) then SKDK is fed into the key derivation function to generate a unique "non-secure" secondary key for use by the crypto engine. When running secure (secure boot; and debug disabled); then SKDK is fed directly to the crypto engine as the secondary key. After the SKDK value has been correctly programmed; the SKDK Read Disable should be blown to permanently protect the SKDK value. Prior to this; the SKDK value can be read from the QFPROM by software. The SBL fuse blow API is capable of automatically generating a random number for use as the SKDK so that the SKDK value is never available outside of the device.
